allowSame.cayley.equationCaption: Pure notation + param placeholders (spanA/sign/spanB/spanSum/a/b/raw/val/n) with no translatable prose; the equation template is identical in every language by design, matching the equation's own notation (mod is a NEUTRAL_TOKEN) — the IDENTICAL-TO-EN finding is a false positive from placeholder names (e.g. spanA) tokenizing as prose words
allowSame.cayley.nLabel: Dutch and Hungarian math terminology borrow "modulus" unchanged from the same Latin root English uses, so "N — modulus" is genuinely identical in nl, hu and en
allowSame.cayley.identityWordAdditive: Italian's, Polish's, both Brazilian and European Portuguese's, and Romanian's word for the additive identity is the genuine cognate "zero" (identical spelling to English), added by quick task 261002-c77 (Italian), extended by quick task 261002-fmi (Polish), quick task 261002-jh4 (Brazilian and European Portuguese), and quick task 261003-0dr (Romanian)

allowLiteral.../Equivalence Wheel/equivalence-wheel.h: updateWheelXref() builds an href string (code), not displayed prose; the cross-link's visible text is the separate static xref element, already translated via cayley.xref
allowLiteral.&lang=: the lang= URL parameter name, appended as code to the same updateWheelXref() href so the cross-link carries the current language, mirroring decorateLinks' own lang= parameter

allowRenderText.N — modulus: Dutch and Hungarian math terminology borrow "modulus" unchanged from the same Latin root English uses, so the rendered nl/hu label is genuinely identical to the English one (same as the dictionary-level allowSame entry for cayley.nLabel above)
